subject: AcreetionOS Update — July 14, 2026
body:
Our continuous integration pipeline just got a significant boost with the implementation of per-pipeline staging directories, which will help avoid publish races between concurrent builds, and relative symlinks for the latest.iso file, making our ISO build process more reliable. This enhancement is a direct result of our community's efforts to refine and stabilize our workflow, ensuring that our users receive the most up-to-date and stable versions of AcreetionOS.

Development
The recent updates to our CI pipeline are a testament to our community's dedication to improving the overall quality of AcreetionOS, and you can learn more about our current workflow at https://acreetionos.org/. Our team is constantly working to refine our processes, and the latest changes will have a positive impact on our users, who can expect more efficient and reliable updates. For more information on our development process, you can visit our changelog page at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html.

Community
The release of Emacs 31.1 has generated a lot of excitement in our community, with many users exploring its new features and capabilities, and we're seeing some interesting discussions on our forums about the potential applications of this new version. Our community is also keeping up with the latest security updates, including the recent stable kernel set, which includes versions 7.1.10 and 6.18.46, and you can find more information on our wiki page at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html. For tips on how to get the most out of AcreetionOS, you can visit our documentation page at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html, and don't forget to check out our flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html for the latest news and updates.
